LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.2 SPEAKING: ETIQUETTE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to observe etiquette?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. pick out the sounds (/ɒ/ and /ɔ: /) and aspects of etiquette in oral or written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. articulate the sounds /ɒ/ and /ɔ: / for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use appropriate etiquette in different contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. justify the need for accurate pronunciation in communication. ● in groups, learners are guided to listen to an oral passage and identify the words with the sounds /ɒ/ and /ɔ: / and note them down, ● in groups, learners are guided to say tongue twisters which have the target sound with peers, ● in groups, learners are guided to present minimal pairs featuring the target sounds and receive peer review, ● in groups, learners with low vision are guided to watch videos using digital devices with assistive technologies while learners with blindness listen to audio clips depicting the use of etiquette in the following instances: o hotels Why is it important to observe etiquette? 5 o telephone conversation o the market among others. ● in pairs, learners with low vision are guided to pick out the polite words and phrases used in the video while learners with blindness pick out the polite words and phrases used in the audio clips and list them, ● in pairs, learners are guided to conduct a telephone conversation using digital devices with assistive technology and observe etiquette, ● in pairs, learners are guided to role play a conversation between a receptionist and a guest, a secretary and a parent in a school or a customer and a seller in a market.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner seeks clarifications as they outline different contexts where business

and market place etiquette is applicable.

● Creativity: The learner undertakes group tasks and gains a new perspective as role play

6

Values:
● Respect: The learner understands and appreciates others as they present minimal pairs featuring the target sounds and

receive peer review.

● Unity: The learner displays team spirit when they jointly practise correct articulation of sounds.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio-economic issues: The learners promote social etiquette as they conduct a telephone conversation using digital devices

with assistive technology on business and market etiquette.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print texts.

● Braille texts.

● Electronic reading materials.

● Digital devices with assistive technology.

● Audio visual clips.

Suggested Skills:

● Picking out the sounds and aspects of etiquette in oral or written texts.

● Articulating target sounds for effective communication.

● Use of appropriate etiquette in different contexts.
